newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE may stretch up towards 4,620.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE may stretch up towards 4,620.

text.p: A bright start to the London stock market on Friday should see the FTSE 100 index extend its gains to around 4,620, technical analysts said.

The market made a bullish engulfing pattern on Thursday when it finished higher than the previous day's intra-day high after dipping below Wednesday's low, so that further gains can be expected, they added.

By 0740 GMT, the FTSE was up 15.5 points at 4,595.9 taking it to the top of trendline resistance formed by a line connecting its intra-day highs since April 16. Breaking above that trendline may make it more unstable, analysts said.

The FTSE has gained eight percent since mid-April making it difficult to maintain this rate of advance. And yet there are no signs of investor insecurity that will call a halt to this uptrend even with the market at its current level.
The implications are that the market will now thrash about making wild swings in an attempt to slow its rate of ascent.

On valuation grounds, the FTSE is currently on a price/earnings ratio of 17 -- and looks slightly stretched -- so if it is to move forward investors must believe the UK economy will keep growing at such a pace that corporate earnings will also grow sufficiently to reduce the ratio.
But as the economy grows, inflationary fears begin to revive leading to thoughts of higher interest rates which will topple the market.
So far these fears have been allayed but it will not take much upset the balance, analysts said.
